content.thinking:
I'm going through the incident timeline: the monthly-spend flag was switched on at 04:20:05Z, and account page requests started failing with a ZeroDivisionError from that point, pushing the error rate up. Argus turned the flag off at 04:26:58, and I'm checking why the failures still show up after that.

I'm now checking the event timeline: even after Argus turned the flag off, evaluations kept returning on and the ZeroDivisionError kept firing, and the service stayed at incident level until the flag was restored. I'm also noting that the earlier client-disconnect errors were background noise and that I'm tracing the causal chain from the failing requests back to the flag.

I'm checking whether the flag is really the cause, since the candidate was refuted, but the record shows evaluations still on after Argus turned the flag off and the errors continued in those same minutes. That suggests the off never reached every evaluation, so I'm tying the flag to the errors through the evaluation counts and the ZeroDivisionError timing from 04:20.

I'm checking the mechanism step: the flag-on path would divide by a count of current-month purchases, which is zero for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month, but that's an unverified assumption, and the log only shows the division at line 47 without the zero condition behind it.

I'm working out the causal chain: the failing requests raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, and the flag-on path divides by the count of this month's purchases, which would be zero for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month. I'm also checking why the errors kept going after the flag was turned off, since evaluations logged as on at 04:28, 04:31 and 04:37 line up with the errors in those same minutes.

I'm comparing the flag's evaluation counts before and after Argus turned it off: the all-off and all-on minutes alternate after the toggle, and the errors only show up in the minutes where evaluations came back on.

I'm working out the stop step now: switching the flag off again, then confirming the ZeroDivisionError lines at spend_summary.py:47 stop appearing in the logs.

I'm noting that the flag-off timing differs between the candidate and the record, and I'm going with the record's 04:26:49Z for Argus's switch. I'm also laying out the contributing factor: no check exercised the flag-on path for shoppers with past purchases but none this month before the flag went on in production.

I'm settling on the contributing factor: no check exercised the flag-on path for shoppers with past purchases but none this month before the flag went on in production, so the proposed item is to require those flag-on paths to run in CI before a flag can be switched on. I'm also noting the flag reached most evaluations from the first minute, so there was no sign of a gradual rollout that would have limited exposure.

I'm adding a third contributing factor: nobody was paged, since the error-rate alert wasn't linked to an on-call incident, so I'm proposing that it be routed to a page. I'm also weighing whether a person paged earlier would have caught that the flag never took effect, and whether the flag-off at 04:26 failing to stop evaluations points to an inconsistent flag state, which I'm still working out.

I'm weighing whether the late alert is a separate contributing factor, but the document already covers that, so I'm leaving it out. The flag-off not reaching evaluations I'll keep under why_it_did_not_help rather than as its own factor, since its cause isn't shown to have existed before the incident.

I'm settling the action items: one gate to run the flag-on tests in CI before a flag goes on in production, and a staged percentage rollout for these flags.

I'm thinking about why io-shop kept logging minutes where every monthly-spend-feature evaluation came back on, even after the flag was switched off at P2. I want to find out whether the off value reached every replica's evaluation, for example through cached or stale provider values, and if it did, why the errors still continued.

I'm moving on to the lessons section, starting with what went well: the investigator tied the onset to the flag toggle, and the mitigation reverted the flag. I'm also weighing whether putting the flag back on after it failed to help counts as a success, since it leaves the flag in a state that keeps the harm going.

I'm weighing whether putting the flag back on was the right call, since the record shows evaluations still returning on after the off toggle, so the revert was judged refuted without confirming the flag ever reached the service. The flag was left on with the failing path, and nobody was paged, which I'll treat as a separate finding.

I'm weighing whether the revert was judged too quickly, since the flag was put back on while the record still showed evaluations returning on after the off toggle. Account pages could keep failing for shoppers who bought before but not this month, with the flag back on and the division unchanged.

I'm drafting the cause-in-plain-words line: a new monthly-spending feature for the shop's account pages exposed a divide-by-zero, most likely for shoppers who have bought before but not this month, so those pages failed. I'm also weighing whether to keep the note that account page requests could keep failing with the flag back on.

I'm writing the root cause: with the flag on, the spend summary divides the month-to-date total by this month's purchase count, and a shopper with no purchases this month hits a zero divisor that turns the account page into a failed request.

I'm settling the wording of the root-cause sentence, checking that I name the file location as given and don't give the count as a number. I'm also making sure the plain-language line doesn't state the error name in a way that changes the meaning.

I'm checking the failure chain now: the account page requests failed, the ZeroDivisionError was raised at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 from the onset onward and not before it, and the error path ran because the monthly-spend feature was on for those shoppers.

I'm checking the rule about earlier changes: the record shows no other change before the incident, so I'm noting that the deploy was ruled out, with no deploy in the read and one revision on every replica, and that the flag toggle was the only change event.

I'm checking the flag-on path for shoppers with past purchases but none this month, and I'm noting that the error came from that path rather than from anything else in the timeline.

I'm drafting the third contributing factor, that nobody was paged, and what a person might have caught sooner, and I'm starting on the action items with the gate to run flag-on tests in CI.

I'm wrapping up the action items: a CI gate that runs flag-on tests before any production flag goes on, staged percentage rollouts with automatic revert when the error rate rises, and routing the error-rate alert to an on-call page. Last, I'm checking how to stop the harm by switching the flag off again and confirming in the logs that no flag-on evaluations remain.

I'm working out the why_it_did_not_help entry: whether the switch-off at P2.1 reached every io-shop flag evaluation, given that minutes still logged evaluations returning on alongside the ZeroDivisionError, and if it did reach them, why the error rate stayed at the incident's level.

I'm checking the went-well and went-wrong items against the record: the Investigator tied the onset to the switch-on, the Mitigation Agent's switch-off could be put back, and the Code-Fix Agent's draft pull request is noted. I'm also weighing whether reverting the flag after the switch-off counts as a failure, since the logs still showed evaluations returning on during the error minutes.

I'm drafting the assumptions list: the claim that the error reached shoppers with past purchases but none this month rests on the Code-Fix reading rather than a log of failed accounts, and the claim that the on-evaluations after the switch-off reflect the served flag value is an assumption I'm recording as such.

action_items.item: Require a passing run of io-shop's tests with a feature flag on before that flag can be switched on in production.
Roll out io-shop feature flags in staged steps, starting with a small share of evaluations.
Halt a flag rollout step automatically when the account page error rate rises during it.
Link ErrorRateSustained on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that it pages a person.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service logged a raised account page error rate.
Those requests failed with ZeroDivisionError raised at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. This error first appears in the logs at the onset and not in the earlier minutes read.

ruled_out.what: A deployment. Deploys were read and none came back, the change events read held only the flag toggle, and all replicas ran one revision.

causal_chain.step: The failing code ran because admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. From that minute most flag evaluations returned on. After the flag was switched off at {P2.1}, the error was logged only in the minutes when evaluations still returned on.
When the flag is on, the code divides by the number of the shopper's purchases in the current month and does not handle the case where there are none.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature for the shop's account pages ran a calculation that fails when a shopper has no purchases in the current month, likely shoppers who have bought before but not this month, so their account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that served the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The failure in the flag-on code would have been found before any shopper's page used it.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: From its first minute, the flag returned on for most evaluations. No smaller staged step was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Fewer shoppers' pages would have failed, and the rise could have been caught and the flag stopped while only a small share of traffic was exposed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: ErrorRateSustained on io-shop was linked to no on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been told when the alert fired and could have stepped in when switching the flag off did not end the failures.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent tied the onset to monthly-spend-feature being switched on.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature off, an action that can be put back.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #559.

went_wrong: The Mitigation Agent judged the switch-off refuted and put monthly-spend-feature back on. Yet the logs after the switch-off showed evaluations still returning on in the same minutes the ZeroDivisionError came, so the flag was left on with the failing code in use.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, which divides the shopper's month-to-date total by the number of purchases in the current month and has no case for when there are none. A shopper who has bought before but not this month brings that number to {F1.1}, so the call raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and `serve_account_page` catches it and returns a failed page.
input.still_at_risk: Account page requests could keep failing with ZeroDivisionError while monthly-spend-feature evaluates on, and switching the flag off might again leave some minutes evaluating on.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at io-shop that every minute's evaluations log monthly-spend-feature=off, with no monthly-spend-feature=on line, and that no account page request fails with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out whether the switch-off at {P2.1} reached every io-shop flag evaluation. After it, the service still logged minutes in which evaluations returned on ({Gce95.5}), with the ZeroDivisionError in the same minutes ({G5309.4}). If the switch-off did reach every evaluation, find out why the service stayed at the incident's level.
